revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Best Deal on Juice Boxes
revealWordProblem.text: The Chef Academy snack bar sells juice boxes in two pack sizes: a 4-pack for $6.00 and a 6-pack for $8.10. Which pack size is the better deal, and how do you know? Explain your reasoning using unit rates.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Find the unit rate (cost per juice box) for each pack. The 4-pack: $6.00 ÷ 4 = $1.50 per juice box. The 6-pack: $8.10 ÷ 6 = $1.35 per juice box. Since $1.35 is less than $1.50, the 6-pack is the better deal.

launch.narrative: It's the final day of Chef Academy — the Culinary Competition! Teams must solve ratio and rate problems to earn ingredients for their dishes. Team 1 needs to figure out how much chicken costs if 3 pounds cost $18. Team 2 must calculate how many cupcakes they can frost if they decorate 5 cupcakes every 4 minutes. The clock is ticking!
noticePrompts: What two quantities with different units are being compared?
How could you find the cost of just 1 pound of chicken?
How could you find the number of cupcakes frosted in 1 minute?
wonderPrompts: Which strategy is fastest — unit rates, ratio tables, or proportions?
What if the rate is not a whole number — can you still solve the problem?

conceptIntro.heading: How do unit rates solve rate problems?
conceptIntro.intro: A rate compares two amounts with different units, like dollars and pounds. A unit rate is the amount for just 1. You find it by dividing, and you can use it to find any amount.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Find the unit rate by dividing, then multiply it to find the amount you need.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: Team 1 knows that 3 pounds of chicken cost $18.
To find the unit rate, I divide the cost by the pounds: 18 divided by 3 = $6 per pound.
Now I can find any amount. For 5 pounds, I multiply: 6 x 5 = $30.
The unit rate $6 per pound is the shortcut for every amount.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: A car drives 100 miles in 2 hours. What is the unit rate in miles per hour?
Divide: 100 divided by 2 = 50 miles per hour.
How far in 4 hours? Multiply: 50 x 4 = 200 miles.

youDo.title: Now it's your turn
lines: Next you will complete the chicken cost table and find the unit rate.
Divide to find the cost of 1 pound, then use it for other amounts.

explore.instructions: Team 1 knows that 3 pounds of chicken cost $18. Complete the ratio table to find the cost for different amounts, then determine the unit rate.

optional.stem: In the kitchen, 3 pizzas feed exactly 12 people. At the same rate, how many pizzas are needed to feed 20 people?
optional.explanation: First find the unit rate: 12 people ÷ 3 pizzas = 4 people per pizza. Then 20 people ÷ 4 people per pizza = 5 pizzas.
choiceFeedback: Re-check how many times you need to multiply or scale.
That would feed more people than the problem asks about. Find how many people one pizza covers, then divide the 20 people by that number.
It looks like the people-per-pizza rate was flipped or skipped. Divide 12 by 3 to see what one pizza covers before dividing 20 by that rate.
optional.stemEs: En la cocina, 3 pizzas alcanzan exactamente para 12 personas. A la misma tasa, ¿cuántas pizzas se necesitan para alimentar a 20 personas?
optional.explanationEs: Primero halla la tasa por unidad: 12 personas ÷ 3 pizzas = 4 personas por pizza. Luego 20 personas ÷ 4 personas por pizza = 5 pizzas.
hints: A unit rate tells you how much one item is worth — here, how many people a single pizza feeds.
Find people per pizza first, then use that rate to see how many pizzas 20 people require.
12 people ÷ 3 pizzas gives 4 people per pizza. Now split the 20 people into groups of that size.
hintsEs: Una tasa por unidad te dice cuánto vale un solo elemento: aquí, para cuántas personas alcanza una pizza.
Halla primero las personas por pizza y luego usa esa tasa para ver cuántas pizzas necesitan 20 personas.
12 personas ÷ 3 pizzas da 4 personas por pizza. Ahora separa a las 20 personas en grupos de ese tamaño.

optional.stem: A line cook chops 8 carrots in 2 minutes. Working at the same steady rate, how many carrots can the cook chop in 7 minutes?
optional.explanation: Unit rate: 8 carrots ÷ 2 minutes = 4 carrots per minute. In 7 minutes: 4 × 7 = 28 carrots.
choiceFeedback: Re-check how many times you need to multiply or scale.
That result uses 8 minutes rather than the 7 the question asks about. Multiply the per-minute rate by exactly 7.
That simply doubles the original 8 carrots instead of using a per-minute rate. Divide 8 by 2 first, then multiply by 7.
optional.stemEs: Un cocinero pica 8 zanahorias en 2 minutos. Trabajando a la misma tasa constante, ¿cuántas zanahorias puede picar en 7 minutos?
optional.explanationEs: Tasa por unidad: 8 zanahorias ÷ 2 minutos = 4 zanahorias por minuto. En 7 minutos: 4 × 7 = 28 zanahorias.
hints: A steady rate means every single minute produces the same number of carrots.
Get the carrots-per-minute rate first, then multiply it by the number of minutes asked about.
8 carrots ÷ 2 minutes gives 4 carrots each minute. Now stretch that rate across all 7 minutes.
hintsEs: Una tasa constante significa que cada minuto produce la misma cantidad de zanahorias.
Obtén primero la tasa de zanahorias por minuto y luego multiplícala por la cantidad de minutos que se pide.
8 zanahorias ÷ 2 minutos da 4 zanahorias cada minuto. Ahora extiende esa tasa a los 7 minutos.

optional.label: Match each kitchen rate to its correct unit rate. Decide what is being compared first.

pairs.term: 24 cups of soup poured into 6 bowls
60 ounces of sauce split into 4 jars

optional.explanation: Divide the first quantity by the second in each card: 24 ÷ 6 = 4 cups per bowl, 30 ÷ 5 = 6 dumplings per plate, 45 ÷ 9 = 5 minutes per cake, and 60 ÷ 4 = 15 ounces per jar. The label on the match tells you which quantity belongs on top before you divide.
optional.explanationEs: Divide la primera cantidad entre la segunda en cada tarjeta: 24 ÷ 6 = 4 tazas por tazón, 30 ÷ 5 = 6 dumplings por plato, 45 ÷ 9 = 5 minutos por pastel y 60 ÷ 4 = 15 onzas por frasco. La etiqueta de la pareja te dice qué cantidad va arriba antes de dividir.
optional.labelEs: Une cada tasa de la cocina con su tasa unitaria correcta. Primero decide qué se está comparando.

optional.stem: Level 2 Extension — Mixed review: A recipe uses 18 ounces of flour to make 3 loaves of bread. How many ounces of flour are needed to make 7 loaves at the same rate?
optional.explanation: Unit rate: 18 ounces ÷ 3 loaves = 6 ounces per loaf. For 7 loaves: 6 × 7 = 42 ounces. The equivalent ratio 18/3 = 42/7 confirms it.
choiceFeedback: Re-check how many times you need to multiply or scale.
That assumes a larger amount of flour per loaf than the recipe gives. Recompute 18 ÷ 3 and then multiply by 7.
That adds a few ounces per extra loaf instead of scaling the whole rate. Find ounces per loaf and multiply by the full 7 loaves.
optional.stemEs: Extensión de Nivel 2 — Repaso mixto: Una receta usa 18 onzas de harina para hacer 3 panes. ¿Cuántas onzas de harina se necesitan para hacer 7 panes a la misma tasa?
optional.explanationEs: Tasa por unidad: 18 onzas ÷ 3 panes = 6 onzas por pan. Para 7 panes: 6 × 7 = 42 onzas. La razón equivalente 18/3 = 42/7 lo confirma.
hints: The recipe keeps the same ratio of flour to loaves no matter how many loaves you bake.
Find the ounces of flour for one loaf, then scale that amount up to 7 loaves.
18 ounces ÷ 3 loaves gives 6 ounces per loaf. Now apply that to all 7 loaves.
hintsEs: La receta mantiene la misma razón de harina a panes sin importar cuántos panes hornees.
Halla las onzas de harina para un solo pan y luego escala esa cantidad a 7 panes.
18 onzas ÷ 3 panes da 6 onzas por pan. Ahora aplícalo a los 7 panes.

optional.title: Level 2 Extension — Catch the Recipe Mistake

workedExample.label: Read the problem
workedExample.work: 9 cups of batter fill 12 muffin cups. How many cups of batter are needed for 16 muffin cups?

workedExample.label: Set up the unit rate
workedExample.work: 12 muffins ÷ 9 cups = about 1.33 muffins per cup

workedExample.label: Answer
workedExample.work: About 21.3 cups of batter are needed

optional.correctWork: The unit rate was set up in the wrong order. Divide cups by muffins: 9 cups ÷ 12 muffins = 0.75 cup per muffin. Then 0.75 × 16 = 12 cups of batter.
hints: Look at Step 2. The question asks for cups of batter, so the unit rate should tell you cups per muffin, not muffins per cup.
Divide 9 cups by 12 muffins to get 0.75 cup per muffin, then multiply by 16 muffins to get 12 cups.
optional.titleEs: Extensión Nivel 2 — Atrapa el error de la receta
optional.explanation: The unit rate step divides 12 muffins by 9 cups, giving muffins per cup when the question asks for cups of batter. Flip the division: 9 ÷ 12 = 0.75 cup per muffin, so 16 muffin cups need 0.75 × 16 = 12 cups of batter — less than the 21.3 the student reported, which should have looked too large.
optional.explanationEs: El paso de la tasa por unidad divide 12 panecillos entre 9 tazas, lo que da panecillos por taza cuando la pregunta pide tazas de masa. Invierte la división: 9 ÷ 12 = 0.75 taza por panecillo, así que 16 moldes necesitan 0.75 × 16 = 12 tazas de masa, menos que las 21.3 que reportó el estudiante, un resultado que debió parecer demasiado grande.

approaching.stem: A bakery makes 24 cookies in 3 batches. What is the unit rate of cookies per batch?
approaching.explanation: Unit rate: 24 cookies ÷ 3 batches = 8 cookies per batch.
choiceFeedback: Re-check how many times you need to multiply or scale.
That is the total number of cookies from all the batches together, not the amount in one batch. A unit rate always describes a single batch, so divide the total by 3.
It looks like the division came out short. Split 24 cookies evenly among the 3 batches again and count how many land in one batch.
hints: 'Per batch' means the number of cookies in exactly ONE batch.
Divide the total cookies by the number of batches to find one batch's share.
Divide 24 cookies by 3 batches — the quotient is your cookies per batch.
approaching.stemEs: Una panadería hace 24 galletas en 3 tandas. ¿Cuál es la tasa por unidad de galletas por tanda?
approaching.explanationEs: Tasa por unidad: 24 galletas ÷ 3 tandas = 8 galletas por tanda.
hintsEs: 'Por tanda' significa el número de galletas de exactamente UNA tanda.
Divide el total de galletas entre el número de tandas para hallar lo que le toca a una tanda.
Divide 24 galletas entre 3 tandas: el cociente son tus galletas por tanda.

approaching.stem: Apples cost $5 for 4 pounds. What is the cost per pound?
choiceFeedback: That is what you get if you divided 4 by 5. Instead: Unit rate: $5 ÷ 4 pounds = ___ per pound.
That price does not come from dividing $5 by 4 pounds. Carry out the division to the exact cents instead of rounding to a friendly number.
That number is the pound count, not a price. Cost per pound comes from dividing the dollars by the pounds.
hints: 'Cost per pound' asks for the dollars for exactly ONE pound.
Divide the total price by the number of pounds. Keep the money on top: dollars ÷ pounds.
Divide 5 ÷ 4 — writing it as 5.00 ÷ 4 can make the decimal easier to see.
approaching.stemEs: Las manzanas cuestan $5 por 4 libras. ¿Cuál es el costo por libra?
approaching.explanationEs: Tasa por unidad: $5 ÷ 4 libras = $1.25 por libra.
hintsEs: 'Costo por libra' pide los dólares de exactamente UNA libra.
Divide el precio total entre el número de libras. Deja el dinero arriba: dólares ÷ libras.
Divide 5 ÷ 4; escribirlo como 5.00 ÷ 4 puede facilitar ver el decimal.

approaching.stem: A cyclist rides 36 miles in 3 hours. At the same rate, how far will she ride in 5 hours?
approaching.explanation: Unit rate: 36 ÷ 3 = 12 miles per hour. In 5 hours: 12 × 5 = 60 miles.
choiceFeedback: Re-check how many times you need to multiply or scale.
That doubles the original 36 miles instead of using the hourly rate. Find miles per hour first, then multiply that rate by 5 hours.
That adds a small fixed amount for each extra hour rather than scaling the rate. Divide 36 by 3 to get miles in one hour, then use all 5 hours.
hints: First find how far she rides in ONE hour, then stretch that out to 5 hours.
Unit rate: miles ÷ hours gives miles per hour. Then multiply that rate by the new time.
Divide 36 ÷ 3 for the miles per hour — then multiply that rate by 5 hours.
approaching.stemEs: Una ciclista recorre 36 millas en 3 horas. A la misma tasa, ¿qué distancia recorrerá en 5 horas?
approaching.explanationEs: Tasa por unidad: 36 ÷ 3 = 12 millas por hora. En 5 horas: 12 × 5 = 60 millas.
hintsEs: Primero halla cuánto recorre en UNA hora y luego extiéndelo a 5 horas.
Tasa unitaria: millas ÷ horas da millas por hora. Luego multiplica esa tasa por el tiempo nuevo.
Divide 36 ÷ 3 para las millas por hora y luego multiplica esa tasa por 5 horas.

approaching.stem: A printer prints 45 pages in 9 minutes. How many pages does it print per minute?
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Unit rate: 45 ÷ 9 = ___.
The quotient is off by one page. Work through 45 ÷ 9 again and check with multiplication before choosing.
That is the total number of pages printed over all 9 minutes, not the amount in a single minute. Divide the total by the minutes.
hints: 'Per minute' means the pages printed in ONE minute.
Divide the pages by the minutes — the result is a pages-per-minute rate.
Divide 45 ÷ 9 to find how many pages print each minute.
approaching.stemEs: Una impresora imprime 45 páginas en 9 minutos. ¿Cuántas páginas imprime por minuto?
approaching.explanationEs: Tasa por unidad: 45 ÷ 9 = 5 páginas por minuto.
hintsEs: 'Por minuto' significa las páginas impresas en UN minuto.
Divide las páginas entre los minutos: el resultado es una tasa de páginas por minuto.
Divide 45 ÷ 9 para hallar cuántas páginas se imprimen cada minuto.

approaching.instructions: Find the unit rate for each situation.
hints: Row 1 shows the move: 120 miles ÷ 4 hours = 30 miles per hour. Copy that thinking in the other rows.
Unit rate = Total ÷ Number of Units. Keep the label, like 'per bottle' or 'per minute.'
For the juice, divide 6.00 ÷ 8 and label it per bottle. Then divide 180 ÷ 3 for the words per minute.
approaching.explanation: A unit rate is the total divided by the number of units, exactly like the model row 120 miles ÷ 4 hours = 30 miles per hour. So the juice is $6.00 ÷ 8 = $0.75 per bottle and the typing is 180 ÷ 3 = 60 words per minute, and each answer keeps a 'per one unit' label.
approaching.explanationEs: Una tasa por unidad es el total dividido entre el número de unidades, igual que en la fila modelo 120 millas ÷ 4 horas = 30 millas por hora. Entonces el jugo da $6.00 ÷ 8 = $0.75 por botella y el tecleo da 180 ÷ 3 = 60 palabras por minuto, y cada respuesta conserva una etiqueta de 'por una unidad'.
approaching.instructionsEs: Encuentra la tasa unitaria de cada situación.
hintsEs: La fila 1 muestra el movimiento: 120 millas ÷ 4 horas = 30 millas por hora. Copia ese razonamiento en las demás filas.
Tasa unitaria = Total ÷ Número de Unidades. Conserva la etiqueta, como 'por botella' o 'por minuto'.
Para el jugo, divide 6.00 ÷ 8 y etiquétalo por botella. Luego divide 180 ÷ 3 para las palabras por minuto.

approaching.title: Spot the Bagel Mistake

workedExample.label: Read the problem
workedExample.work: A bakery sells 4 bagels for $6. How much do 12 bagels cost at the same rate?

approaching.correctWork: The unit rate of $1.50 per bagel is correct, but you multiply to find the total, not add: $1.50 × 12 = $18. So 12 bagels cost $18.
hints: Look at Step 3. The unit rate $1.50 per bagel is right — but what operation finds the cost of 12 bagels?
To find a total from a unit rate, multiply: $1.50 × 12 = $18, not $1.50 + 12.
approaching.titleEs: Detecta el error de los bagels
approaching.explanation: The unit rate $6 ÷ 4 = $1.50 per bagel is right, but the next step writes $1.50 + 12. A unit rate tells you the cost of one bagel, so 12 bagels cost $1.50 × 12 = $18.
approaching.explanationEs: La tasa por unidad $6 ÷ 4 = $1.50 por bagel está bien, pero el siguiente paso escribe $1.50 + 12. Una tasa por unidad te dice cuánto cuesta un bagel, así que 12 bagels cuestan $1.50 × 12 = $18.

onLevel.instructions: Team 2 frosts 5 cupcakes every 4 minutes. Complete the ratio table to find how many cupcakes they can frost in different times.
hints: The base row is 5 cupcakes every 4 minutes. Every other row is a multiple of those 4 minutes.
Find each row's scale factor (minutes ÷ 4), then multiply 5 cupcakes by that factor.
For 8 minutes: divide 8 ÷ 4 for the factor, then multiply 5 cupcakes by it. Use the same idea for 12 and 20 minutes.
onLevel.explanation: The base row is 5 cupcakes in 4 minutes, so every later row scales both numbers by the same factor: 8 minutes is 2 × 4 → 10 cupcakes, 12 minutes is 3 × 4 → 15 cupcakes, and 20 minutes is 5 × 4 → 25 cupcakes. The ratio 5 : 4 stays constant down the whole table.
onLevel.explanationEs: La fila base es 5 pastelitos en 4 minutos, así que cada fila siguiente escala ambos números por el mismo factor: 8 minutos es 2 × 4 → 10 pastelitos, 12 minutos es 3 × 4 → 15 pastelitos y 20 minutos es 5 × 4 → 25 pastelitos. La razón 5 : 4 se mantiene constante en toda la tabla.
onLevel.instructionsEs: El equipo 2 decora 5 pastelitos cada 4 minutos. Completa la tabla de razones para encontrar cuántos pastelitos pueden decorar en distintos tiempos.
hintsEs: La fila base son 5 pastelitos cada 4 minutos. Todas las demás filas son múltiplos de esos 4 minutos.
Halla el factor de escala de cada fila (minutos ÷ 4) y luego multiplica los 5 pastelitos por ese factor.
Para 8 minutos: divide 8 ÷ 4 para el factor y luego multiplica 5 pastelitos por él. Usa la misma idea para 12 y 20 minutos.

onLevel.stem: A car travels 150 miles in 3 hours. A bus travels 200 miles in 5 hours. Which vehicle is faster?
onLevel.explanation: Car: 150÷3 = 50 mph. Bus: 200÷5 = 40 mph. The car travels faster at 50 mph vs. 40 mph.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Car: 150÷3 = 50 mph.
The distances and the times are both different, so equal speed cannot be assumed. Divide each distance by its own time and compare the two unit rates.
There is enough information here — each vehicle gives both a distance and a time. Turn each pair into miles per hour and the comparison becomes clear.
hints: You can't compare 150 miles and 200 miles directly — the travel times are different.
Find each vehicle's speed in miles per ONE hour: divide miles by hours, then compare the two speeds.
Car: divide 150 ÷ 3. Bus: divide 200 ÷ 5. The bigger miles-per-hour value belongs to the faster vehicle.
onLevel.stemEs: Un carro recorre 150 millas en 3 horas. Un autobús recorre 200 millas en 5 horas. ¿Cuál vehículo es más rápido?
onLevel.explanationEs: Carro: 150 ÷ 3 = 50 mph. Autobús: 200 ÷ 5 = 40 mph. El carro va más rápido, a 50 mph frente a 40 mph.
hintsEs: No puedes comparar 150 millas y 200 millas directamente: los tiempos de viaje son distintos.
Halla la velocidad de cada vehículo en millas por UNA hora: divide millas entre horas y luego compara las dos velocidades.
Carro: divide 150 ÷ 3. Autobús: divide 200 ÷ 5. El valor mayor de millas por hora es del vehículo más rápido.

onLevel.instructions: Sort each rate problem by the strategy that works BEST to solve it.

items.text: Find cost per pound when 5 lb costs $12
If 3 shirts cost $24, find cost of 9 shirts
A car goes 55 mph — how far in 4 hours?
Scale a recipe from 4 servings to 20 servings

onLevel.hint: Read each item carefully and sort by the comparison type.
hints: Ask each card: do I need the amount for ONE unit, or am I scaling a group up to a bigger group?
'Per pound' or 'per hour' wording points to unit rate. Jumping from one group size to another (like 3 shirts → 9) fits a ratio table.
Test the first card: 'cost per pound when 5 lb costs $12' literally asks for a per-ONE-pound amount. Which strategy is that?
onLevel.explanation: 'Cost per pound when 5 lb costs $12' and 'a car goes 55 mph — how far in 4 hours?' both hinge on the amount for ONE unit, so they belong under Use Unit Rate. The shirts card (3 → 9) and the recipe card (4 servings → 20) scale a whole group up, which a ratio table handles directly.
onLevel.explanationEs: «Costo por libra cuando 5 lb cuestan $12» y «un carro va a 55 mph, ¿cuánto recorre en 4 horas?» dependen de la cantidad por UNA unidad, así que van en Usar tasa por unidad. La tarjeta de las camisas (3 → 9) y la de la receta (4 porciones → 20) escalan un grupo completo, y eso lo resuelve directo una tabla de razones.
onLevel.instructionsEs: Clasifica cada problema de tasas según la estrategia que funciona MEJOR para resolverlo.
hintsEs: Pregúntale a cada tarjeta: ¿necesito la cantidad de UNA unidad o estoy escalando un grupo a un grupo mayor?
Palabras como 'por libra' o 'por hora' apuntan a tasa unitaria. Saltar de un tamaño de grupo a otro (como 3 camisas → 9) encaja con una tabla de razones.
Prueba la primera tarjeta: 'costo por libra si 5 lb cuestan $12' pide literalmente la cantidad de UNA libra. ¿Qué estrategia es esa?

onLevel.label: A runner goes 6 miles in 48 minutes. Place markers showing distance at 0, 16, 32, and 48 minutes.
hints: Notice the tick marks count by 8s from 0 to 48, and the runner keeps a steady pace the whole way.
16 minutes is one-third of the 48, so she has covered one-third of her 6 miles by then. Each 16-minute chunk adds the same distance.
Place '0 mi' at 0 first. Then count ticks: 16 is two ticks of 8, so the '2 mi' marker goes there. Keep that pattern going.
onLevel.explanation: The runner covers 6 miles in 48 minutes, a steady 1 mile every 8 minutes. So the markers land at 0 min → 0 mi, 16 min → 2 mi, 32 min → 4 mi, and 48 min → 6 mi, with the distance growing by 2 miles for each 16-minute jump.
onLevel.explanationEs: La corredora recorre 6 millas en 48 minutos, un ritmo constante de 1 milla cada 8 minutos. Por eso los marcadores quedan en 0 min → 0 mi, 16 min → 2 mi, 32 min → 4 mi y 48 min → 6 mi, y la distancia crece 2 millas en cada salto de 16 minutos.

onLevel.title: Spot the Smoothie Mistake

workedExample.label: Read the problem
workedExample.work: A smoothie stand makes 18 smoothies in 6 minutes. How many smoothies can it make in 10 minutes at the same rate?

onLevel.correctWork: The unit rate was divided in the wrong order. The question asks for smoothies, so find smoothies per minute: 18 smoothies ÷ 6 minutes = 3 smoothies per minute. Then 3 × 10 = 30 smoothies in 10 minutes.
hints: Look at Step 2. The question asks how many smoothies, so the unit rate should be smoothies per minute, not minutes per smoothie.
Divide 18 smoothies by 6 minutes to get 3 smoothies per minute, then multiply by 10 minutes to get 30 smoothies.
onLevel.explanation: The unit rate step divides 6 minutes by 18 smoothies, which answers 'how long per smoothie' when the question asks how many smoothies. Put the quantity you want on top: 18 ÷ 6 = 3 smoothies per minute, so 3 × 10 = 30 smoothies in 10 minutes.
onLevel.explanationEs: El paso de la tasa por unidad divide 6 minutos entre 18 batidos, lo cual responde «cuánto tiempo por batido» cuando la pregunta es cuántos batidos. Coloca arriba la cantidad que buscas: 18 ÷ 6 = 3 batidos por minuto, así que 3 × 10 = 30 batidos en 10 minutos.

extending.title: Find Mia's Mistake

workedExample.label: Read the problem
workedExample.work: A store sells 6 oranges for $4.50. What is the cost of 10 oranges?

hints: Look at Step 3. Mia found the correct unit rate of $0.75, but what did she do with it?
To find the total cost, you multiply the unit rate by the number of items — not add.
extending.explanation: Mia's unit rate $4.50 ÷ 6 = $0.75 per orange is correct, but she then wrote $0.75 + 10 instead of multiplying. Ten oranges at $0.75 each cost $0.75 × 10 = $7.50.
extending.explanationEs: La tasa por unidad de Mía, $4.50 ÷ 6 = $0.75 por naranja, está correcta, pero luego escribió $0.75 + 10 en lugar de multiplicar. Diez naranjas a $0.75 cada una cuestan $0.75 × 10 = $7.50.

extending.stem: A factory makes 240 widgets in 8 hours. Another factory makes 200 widgets in 5 hours. Which factory is faster? If both factories work together for 10 hours, how many total widgets would they produce?
extending.sampleAnswer: Factory A: 240 ÷ 8 = 30 widgets/hour. Factory B: 200 ÷ 5 = 40 widgets/hour. Factory B is faster. Together: (30 + 40) × 10 = 70 × 10 = 700 widgets in 10 hours.
extending.hint: Remember to explain which type each ratio is.
hints: There are two questions: which factory is faster, AND the combined total for 10 hours.
Find each factory's widgets per hour (widgets ÷ hours). For the team-up, add the two rates before multiplying by 10.
Factory A: divide 240 ÷ 8 for its hourly rate. Then find Factory B's rate with 200 ÷ 5 and compare before you combine them.
extending.stemEs: Una fábrica produce 240 aparatos en 8 horas. Otra fábrica produce 200 aparatos en 5 horas. ¿Cuál fábrica es más rápida? Si ambas fábricas trabajan juntas durante 10 horas, ¿cuántos aparatos producirían en total?
extending.explanation: Each factory's speed is its unit rate: 240 ÷ 8 = 30 widgets per hour and 200 ÷ 5 = 40 widgets per hour, so the second factory is faster. Working together their combined rate is 30 + 40 = 70 widgets per hour, and over 10 hours that is 70 × 10 = 700 widgets.
extending.explanationEs: La rapidez de cada fábrica es su tasa por unidad: 240 ÷ 8 = 30 aparatos por hora y 200 ÷ 5 = 40 aparatos por hora, así que la segunda fábrica es más rápida. Trabajando juntas, su tasa combinada es 30 + 40 = 70 aparatos por hora, y en 10 horas eso da 70 × 10 = 700 aparatos.
hintsEs: Hay dos preguntas: cuál fábrica es más rápida Y el total combinado en 10 horas.
Halla los artículos por hora de cada fábrica (artículos ÷ horas). Para el trabajo en equipo, suma las dos tasas antes de multiplicar por 10.
Fábrica A: divide 240 ÷ 8 para su tasa por hora. Luego halla la tasa de la Fábrica B con 200 ÷ 5 y compara antes de combinarlas.

extending.instructions: Two delivery services charge different rates. Service A: $3 per mile + $5 flat fee. Service B: $4 per mile, no flat fee. Complete the table and determine when each is cheaper.
hints: Service A always adds a $5 flat fee on top of $3 per mile; Service B is just $4 per mile with no fee.
For each mileage row: A = 3 × miles + 5, and B = 4 × miles. Then compare the two costs to fill the cheaper-option column.
For 2 miles: work out 3 × 2 + 5 for Service A and 4 × 2 for Service B. Compare them, then repeat for 5 and 10 miles.
extending.explanation: Service A costs 3 × miles + 5 and Service B costs 4 × miles, so at 2 miles A = $11 and B = $8, at 5 miles both are $20, and at 10 miles A = $35 while B = $40. B wins on short trips because A's $5 flat fee dominates, they tie at 5 miles, and after that A's cheaper $3 per mile takes over.
extending.explanationEs: El Servicio A cuesta 3 × millas + 5 y el Servicio B cuesta 4 × millas, así que a 2 millas A = $11 y B = $8, a 5 millas ambos dan $20, y a 10 millas A = $35 mientras B = $40. B gana en viajes cortos porque la tarifa fija de $5 de A pesa mucho, se empatan en 5 millas, y de ahí en adelante manda el precio más bajo de $3 por milla de A.
extending.instructionsEs: Dos servicios de entrega cobran tarifas diferentes. Servicio A: $3 por milla + $5 de cuota fija. Servicio B: $4 por milla, sin cuota fija. Completa la tabla y determina cuándo conviene cada uno.
hintsEs: El Servicio A siempre suma una tarifa fija de $5 sobre $3 por milla; el Servicio B es solo $4 por milla sin tarifa.
Para cada fila de millas: A = 3 × millas + 5 y B = 4 × millas. Luego compara los dos costos para llenar la columna de la opción más barata.
Para 2 millas: calcula 3 × 2 + 5 para el Servicio A y 4 × 2 para el Servicio B. Compáralos y luego repite con 5 y 10 millas.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Ratio and Rate Problem Solving is dividing in the wrong order when setting up the unit rate — for example, finding "minutes per smoothie" (6 ÷ 18) instead of "smoothies per minute" (18 ÷ 6) — or using addition instead of multiplication to scale the unit rate, like adding $0.75 + 10 instead of multiplying $0.75 × 10. Before you submit, check: does your unit rate match the units the question is asking for, and did you multiply (not add) to scale it to the new amount?

diagram.title: Runner's Pace Scales by Miles
diagram.caption: Each bar is minutes to run that many miles at 9 min per mile; the bars grow evenly, so the 5K (3.1 mi) is predicted at about 27.9 min.

connect.scenario: A runner trains for a 5K race. During practice, she runs 3 miles in 27 minutes. She wants to know her pace (minutes per mile) and predict how long the full 5K (3.1 miles) will take at the same rate.
connect.prompt: This is like our rate problem-solving work because ___ and ___ are related by ___.

check.stem: What is the runner's pace in minutes per mile?
At that pace, about how long will the 3.1-mile 5K take?
Why is the 5K time only a little more than 27 minutes?
choices: Because the extra 0.1 mile adds only about 0.9 minute
Because the pace speeds up over longer distances
check.explanation: The extra 0.1 mile takes 0.1 × 9 = 0.9 minute, so the total is 27 + 0.9 = 27.9 minutes.

connect.modelAnswer: The unit rate is 27 ÷ 3 = 9 minutes per mile. At that pace the 3.1-mile 5K takes 3.1 × 9 = 27.9 minutes, just under 28 minutes.

exitTicket.stem: A printer prints 30 pages in 5 minutes. At this rate, how many pages will it print in 12 minutes?
exitTicket.explanation: Unit rate: 30 ÷ 5 = 6 pages per minute. In 12 minutes: 6 × 12 = 72 pages.
choiceFeedback: That's 10 minutes' worth — find the rate per minute first.
Find pages per minute (30 ÷ 5), then multiply by 12.
You may have added — use the unit rate times 12 minutes.
hints: 12 minutes isn't a neat multiple of 5 minutes, so find the pages printed in ONE minute first.
Unit rate: divide the 30 pages by the 5 minutes, then multiply that rate by 12 minutes.
Divide 30 ÷ 5 for the pages per minute — then multiply that rate by 12.

questions.stem: A printer prints 45 pages in 9 minutes. How many pages does it print per minute?
A cyclist rides 36 miles in 3 hours. At the same rate, how far will she ride in 5 hours?
questions.explanation: Unit rate: 36 ÷ 3 = 12 miles per hour. In 5 hours: 12 × 5 = 60 miles.

questions.stem: Apples cost $5 for 4 pounds. What is the cost per pound?
A bakery makes 24 cookies in 3 batches. What is the unit rate of cookies per batch?
questions.explanation: Unit rate: 24 cookies ÷ 3 batches = 8 cookies per batch.
